claim: Bending stiffness EI of corrugated PP twinwall per unit width can be estimated per flute direction from grammage
law: Sandwich section (two skins plus ribs, skins sized from grammage at 886 kg/m3) fitted to Akyplac ISO 178 three-point flexural rigidity (k = 48 EI / L^3, L 100 mm, b 40 mm); CD from the measured CD/MD ratio, log-interpolated in thickness
check: Fitted E_eff 1249 MPa, above the raw resin (1100 to 1150 MPa), so the section model under-counts I or the skins are oriented: EI is a fitted effective value, not a bound; within 7 % of both data points. 4 mm FR 700: EI_MD 2,621, EI_CD 766 N mm2/mm; at -10 % grammage 2,390 and 699. EI_CD at a 100 mm span is shear-dominated, so it under-states CD bending at 600 mm spans (conservative there); 4 to 10 mm values are interpolated, not measured
closed_by: T1: ISO 178 on the bought lot, both directions, at 100 and 400 mm spans, 23 and 50 C

claim: Every platform panel above 600 mm stands only with both vertical edges supported (fold or angle joint of 30 deg or more, corner or tee)
law: Greenhill self-weight buckling h_cr = (7.837 EI / q)^(1/3), strip clamped at the base (an upper bound: a foot is not a clamp)
check: Flat 4 mm FR: h_cr 1441 mm cold, 1144 mm hot (x 0.5 stiffness); a flat P12 strip has a load margin of 1.73 cold and 0.87 hot, a flat P18 strip fails outright; 10 % lighter sheet lowers h_cr by about 3 %. Fixed by rule S1 for every panel above 600 mm (P12 included); the supported leaf is P3
closed_by: Fix F1 (rule S1, v0.2: P12 included, angle clip)

claim: A 600 mm leaf supported on both vertical edges carries its own weight at 1800 mm without buckling, cold and hot
law: Orthotropic plate, uniform compression, long plate: N_cr = pi^2/b^2 (2 sqrt(D1 D2) + 2 D3), D3 = 0 as the lower bound (twinwall is soft in twist); against N = q H at the base
check: Margin 3.1 cold and 1.6 hot, load factor 2 included, at D3 = 0 (v0.1 used k = 4 and gave 6.3; uniform base load is conservative). An edge at a 30 deg fold or angle clip is held laterally by the next leaf's in-plane stiffness x sin 30 = 0.5, which is far stiffer than the restraint buckling needs, but this is not computed here
closed_by: Rule S1; T1 hot and T7 bay test at 23 and 50 C

claim: Panels are boundaries, not barriers: a 600 mm leaf bows well past 25 mm under the 178 N BIFMA push
law: w = alpha P b^2 / D (simply supported on four edges, a/b = 3, alpha 0.0169), D = sqrt(D_MD D_CD); a free top edge is worse
check: 4 mm FR: 764 mm at 178 N (small-deflection theory; membrane action limits it); 25 mm at 5.8 N. 10 mm: 88 mm. No twinwall grade resists a hand push in bending; the claim is dropped and stated as limit L1
closed_by: D5 Proposed, awaiting Amish: stated limit L1 in every product

claim: Platform panels, standing in their feet, top out below 1829 mm, outside the scope of the IBC interior partition load (780 CMR 1607.13)
law: Top = 1800 mm panel + 10.5 mm foot seat = 1810.5 mm, margin 18.5 mm before tolerances (sheet length 0 to +1 in on standard sheets is trimmed off). Outside the threshold removes one load case only; it is not evidence of strength (a 4 mm leaf would deflect about 268 mm under 0.24 kN/m2); BIFMA and the authority having jurisdiction still apply
closed_by: Rule S2 (cut height tolerance 0 to -3 mm)

claim: No platform layout relies on a single freestanding panel
law: Overturning about the outrigger tip: F = W a / z
check: A flat P18 duo on two standard feet tips at 6.1 N against the 178 N BIFMA push; it would need 40 kg of ballast per foot. Fixed by rule S3 (L, U or closed plans only)
closed_by: Fix F2 (rule S3)

claim: A zigzag U bay (2.3 m back and returns of P18 duos) with a 5 kg bag at each far return foot does not tip under the 178 N push
law: Restoring moment of returns, feet and ballast about the back wall base line, push at 1372 mm; the U is taken as rigid
check: Unballasted 77 N; ballast needed 3.1 kg per far foot; with 5 kg 242 N. Not modelled: the push reaches the returns through a leaf that bows (P4) and clips (P9), so the rigid-U figure is an upper bound on what the bay resists before a joint lets go; BIFMA 5.1 also asks for no loss of serviceability
closed_by: Fix F2 (rule S3, zigzag walls in v0.2); T7 bay test

claim: A bay slides on the floor before it tips under a push
law: Sliding F = mu W against the tipping force of P7
check: Ballasted U bay 23.3 kg: slides at 57 N if mu = 0.25 (ASSUMED; floor and pad friction not cited); it can only tip if mu exceeds 1.06. Sliding caps the tipping load, which helps, but a bay that slides moves zone lines
closed_by: D17 Proposed, awaiting Amish: accept sliding or add non-slip pads; T7 measures mu

claim: The ballasted bay does not tip under the BIFMA X5.6 5.2 impact (22.7 kg bag, 610 mm horizontal swing)
law: Energy to rotate the bay over its tipping line (raise of centres of mass) against the bag's energy
check: Tipping needs about 295 J; the bag's energy depends on its pendulum length, which the report does not give (the reviewer's 34 J is not cited): to assess. Local damage to the struck leaf is not covered
closed_by: T7 impact case

claim: The platform is for indoor use or use inside a tent
law: q = 0.5 rho v^2, Cp 1.0 ASSUMED, resultant at mid-height; no gust factor
check: 10 m/s gives 61 Pa and 238 N m on a 2.4 x 1.8 m wall; the ballasted U restores 333 N m, under 1.5 x the wind moment. Outdoor use fails; tent door gusts and fans are not checked
closed_by: D6 Proposed, awaiting Amish: indoor or in-tent only (stated limit L2)

claim: Clips hold the panel edges under the 178 N BIFMA push (no separation)
law: Bearing d t sigma_y per skin, tear-out 2 e t tau; demand from a bowed leaf as a string T = P L / (4 delta)
check: v0.1 peg (3.7 mm) reached the near skin only: 44 N per peg, refuted. v0.2 through-peg (fix F8) bears on both skins: 88 N per peg, 176 N per clip. Demand is not bounded on paper: 162 N per clip if two of three clips share the v0.1 estimate (324 N per edge, delta 165 mm is a BIFMA stop, not a sag), up to 1158 N per edge if the leaf acts as a string with held edges (delta 23 mm). Thin FR skins may crumple before full bearing
closed_by: Fix F8 (through-peg); D14 Proposed, awaiting Amish: holding principle settled by T3 and T7

claim: The PETG through-peg does not shear before the panel hole yields
law: Peg shear pi d^2 / 4 x 50.4 / sqrt 3 MPa (BCN3D), derated x 0.3 for layers across the peg (ASSUMED); the peg is printed with the tongue lying flat

claim: The tapered snap tongue deflects by the full through-peg height (5.5 mm) below half the PETG strain at yield, root factor included
law: Bayer tapered arm eps = y h / (1.09 l^2), l 24.5 mm, h 1.5 to 0.75 mm, x 2.0 at the root (ASSUMED). At rest the peg sits in its socket and the tongue is unstrained (no creep); slot gap 4.5 mm takes sheet of 3.8 to 4.2 mm (+-5 %)
check: 2.52188 % strain <= 2.95 % strain
closed_by: Moulded PP strain limit to assess (D4); T3 cycles; print the tongue lying flat

claim: Clipping and release are tool-free with gloved hands: push the panel home; release with two fingertips on the two lips while the other hand pulls
law: Bayer: P = b h^2 E eps / (6 l); insertion over a 45 deg ramp that covers the whole peg height, P (mu + 1)/(1 - mu), mu 0.45 (PP on PP x 1.5)
check: Deflection 5.5 N per tongue; insertion about 29 N per slot pushed through the panel edge; release 5.5 N per lip over 5.5 mm. The v0.1 peg (1.2 mm lead-in on a 3.7 mm peg) could not cam and was refuted; no cited hand-force limit is used, and the two-handed method is stated
closed_by: Fix F9 (full-height ramp); T5 with gloved users

claim: The flat-bottomed fold groove (front skin only) folds 180 deg for flat-pack and +-90 deg either way in use
law: Back to back the skin wraps a radius R = t - t_s/2 and needs pi R of free skin; strain t_s/(2R)
check: R 3.87 mm needs 12.2 mm of free skin: the v0.1 groove (10.2 mm) stopped at about 150 deg; v0.2 groove 13.6 mm (4 pitches, flat-bottomed) gives 3.4 % at 180 deg and 1.5 % at 90 deg the other way. Raw PP elongation at yield is 11 % (Akyplac); FR fillers and cross orientation lower it: to assess. Routing depth tolerance to assess
closed_by: Fix F3 (groove 4 pitches, flat bottom, two-way); T2 at 5, 23 and 50 C

claim: Folds and clip joints survive 50 to 100 deployment cycles with at least 80 % of their first retention
law: Low-cycle fatigue of PP and PETG at the strains of P11 and P13; hole wear in a 0.26 mm skin
check: Hinge 3.4 % per fold, tongue 2.5 % at the root per cycle; no data for scored FR twinwall or printed PETG tongues; holes ovalise with each cycle; the 80 % retention target is ASSUMED: to assess
closed_by: T2 and T3 (with hole wear and retention per cycle) at TRL 4

claim: Standard modules cut from a 48 x 96 in (1219.2 x 2438.4 mm) sheet with under 5 % waste
law: Area of modules / sheet area; width trim 9.6 mm per side nominal, about 8.0 mm after the -1/8 in width tolerance; squareness is set by cutting to a square datum, not by the trim
check: 96.8752 % yield >= 95 % yield

claim: One person carries a folded P18 duo under the arm, held horizontal
law: Mass against the NIOSH load constant (23 kg) as a ceiling only: NIOSH is a two-handed lifting method; a 1.8 m fold cannot be carried hanging from one hand (its end would reach the floor); wind area 1.08 m2 outdoors

claim: A 12 kg two-bag pack (FlexTriage deck target) holds a 2.3 x 2.3 m zigzag U bay of P18 duos
law: Sum of panel, foot, clip and bag masses (ballast filled on site)
check: 6 duos 9.07 kg + 7 feet 3.22 kg + 15 clips 1.01 kg + bags 1.0 kg = 14.3 kg, 19 % over 12 kg (the v0.1 row counted 6 feet and read Plausible: refuted). Cored feet of 0.15 kg and clips of 0.04 kg (ASSUMED targets) would give 11.7 kg
closed_by: D15 Proposed, awaiting Amish: pack target, bag count or lighter moulded feet and clips

claim: PP sheet tolerates 0.5 % sodium hypochlorite, 70 % alcohol and 3 to 7.5 % hydrogen peroxide at the label contact time
law: CP Lab: NaOCl < 20 % A, ethanol A, isopropyl A2 (satisfactory to 48 C), H2O2 10 % A; INEOS: NaOCl conc. S at 21 C, O at 60 C; H2O2 30 % S/O
check: Resin immersion data only: the Akyplac sheet itself says PP is not resistant to oxidising substances, and oxidisers attack UV stabilisers; the FR additive, print and tent temperatures of 40 to 50 C are not covered
closed_by: T4 at 23 and 45 C with 0.5 % NaOCl, 70 % alcohol, a named quat and accelerated H2O2 at label contact times

claim: PP sheet tolerates quaternary ammonium disinfectants
law: Neither chart lists quats; CP Lab rates detergents A
check: Uncited: to assess with a named quat product's maker list
closed_by: T4

claim: PETG prototype clips tolerate 0.5 % sodium hypochlorite, 70 % isopropanol and 3 to 5 % hydrogen peroxide
law: Curbell (Vivak, flat unstressed sheet): diluted bleach (5 tablespoons per gallon, about 2 % household bleach, 0.10 to 0.16 % NaOCl), IPA 70 %, H2O2 3 to 5 % compatible; quats not listed
check: 0.5 % NaOCl is about 3 to 5 times the tested strength and printed parts trap fluid between layers: to assess. The v0.2 tongue is unstrained at rest, which lowers the stress-cracking risk
closed_by: T4 on printed clips; moulded PP clips at scale fall under P18

claim: Printed pictograms stay legible after repeated disinfectant wipes
law: No wipe data for UV inks on twinwall; Fujifilm Uvijet KX lists Coroplast as variable, full resistance 24 h after cure
check: To assess (no evidence either way). Proposed protection: clear PP overlaminate (D3)
closed_by: T4: 120 wipes, 30 min dry per agent, legibility scored

claim: Sealed panel edges, fold grooves and clip holes can be wiped clean between uses
law: Open flute ends, cut edges parallel to the flutes (open half-flute troughs), the open back-face groove and clip slots are crevices
check: Fixed by rule E1 v0.2 (every cut edge heat-sealed, including the two groove shoulders and the groove ends; hot-punched fused holes), rule E2 (groove face away from care zones or covered by a flexible PP strip) and rule E3 (clips come off for cleaning); seal integrity unproven
closed_by: Fix F4 (rules E1 to E3); T6 dye ingress after T4

claim: Twinwall panels are combustible and add fire load to a care space; the FR grade does not reduce that fire load
law: Heat of combustion 39.7 MJ/kg (FSRI PP)
check: 27.8 MJ/m2; 60 MJ per P18 duo; 360 MJ per six-duo U bay. FR delays ignition and spread; PP still melts and drips (P39)
closed_by: Rule FR1: FR grade only near people

claim: The platform FR grade is bought at a measured lot areal density of at most 700 g/m2 (NFPA 701 TM1 scope)
law: NFPA 701 TM1 applies to areal density <= 700 g/m2 (IntePro); grammage tolerance +-5 to +-10 %, so the nominal is at most about 665 g/m2 and the lot is weighed
check: 700 g/m2 (lot maximum) <= 700 g/m2 (lot maximum)
closed_by: Fix F5 v0.2 (lot maximum, not nominal); D18 Proposed, awaiting Amish: benchmark hierarchy (NFPA 286 or ASTM E84 first, NFPA 701 second)

claim: An FR twinwall grade can reach a European reaction-to-fire class (EN 13501-1)
law: UK FR boards cite LPS 1207 only
check: No twinwall classification found; the FR solid film report (B-s2,d0 on a metal frame with an air gap) is a different product and mounting and is not evidence: to assess
closed_by: D2: target class set by Amish after supplier quotes

claim: Zone colours are read correctly by staff with red-green colour vision deficiency
law: Red-green deficiency about 1 in 12 men and 1 in 200 women of Northern European ancestry (MedlinePlus)
check: Colour alone fails; fixed by rule C1 (text, shape and pattern with every colour); legibility unproven
closed_by: Fix F6 (rule C1); T5 with colour-deficient observers

claim: Panels, folds and clips keep their function at 40 to 50 C inside a tent
law: Akyplac HDT 50 C at 1.8 MPa and 92 C at 0.45 MPa; PETG HDT 70 C (BCN3D); stiffness x 0.5 ASSUMED hot with creep
check: Hot: flat P12 margin 0.87 (rule S1 covers it), leaf margin 1.6, U bay tip unchanged (weight, not stiffness); fold set angles may relax; PETG clips stay below their HDT but near it in sun
closed_by: T1, T2, T7 at 50 C

claim: Folds and clips do not crack in cold use (5 C and below)
law: Akyplac Izod (ISO 180) 15 kJ/m2 at 23 C, 7 kJ/m2 at -20 C
check: Toughness halves by -20 C; no data at 5 C for scored skins or printed tongues: to assess; platform use below 5 C is not claimed
closed_by: T2 and T3 at 5 C

claim: Thermal expansion of a 2.4 m wall is taken up without bowing off its feet
law: Akyprint 0.11 mm/(m C); zigzag wall with leaves at 15 deg
check: 7.9 mm over a 30 C swing on 2.4 m; the zigzag takes it with a fold angle change of about 0.7 deg; slot clearance 0.15 to 0.35 mm per side does not need to
closed_by: Rule S1 (zigzag walls)

claim: Panels keep their properties over a stated service life
law: Akyprint 'UV treatment internal 18 months'; Interprofile outdoor grade 2,500 h SAE J1960, about 1 year in Miami
check: Indoor use only (L2); no service life is claimed; sunlit tent walls and the effect of brominated FR on UV stabilisers: to assess
closed_by: D6; supplier data for the FR plus UV grade

claim: Static charge on PP panels is acceptable near medical electronics and oxygen use
law: Akyplac: anti-static on request; Interprofile antistatic grade 1e9 to 1e12 ohm/sq
check: Standard PP is highly insulating; dust pick-up and discharge near oxygen-enriched areas: to assess with the site; anti-static FR availability to assess
closed_by: Site review; supplier data

claim: Edges, grooves and folds do not cut or pinch fingers
law: Sealed (fused) edges; 0.26 mm skins at routed shoulders; folds close fully only when packing
check: Sealed edges are rounded; routed shoulders are sealed by rule E1; pinch at a closing fold only during packing (hands on the leaf faces). Sharp-edge test (UL 1439 type) planned
closed_by: T5 sharp-edge and pinch check

claim: Sheet of 3.8 to 4.2 mm (+-5 %) fits the 4.5 mm clip slot and the through-peg engages at both extremes
law: Slot gap 4.5 mm; peg passes both skins into a 1.0 mm socket whatever the sheet position
check: 4.2 mm sheet vs slot <= 4.5 mm sheet vs slot
closed_by: Fix F8 (CLEAR 0.5 mm)

claim: Zone colours and safety signs do not conflict
law: ISO 3864-1 reserves red, yellow, blue and green for safety meanings; START triage uses red, yellow, green and black (CHEMM)
check: Triage red and green collide with fire-equipment red and safe-condition green in one bay. Fixed by rule C6 (triage colours only as zone bands carrying the category word, never as sign backgrounds; safety signs keep ISO shapes and borders). ISO 3864-4 colour values and the sign-size distance factor are not yet read from the standards (the reviewer's z = 60 is unverified): to assess
closed_by: Fix F10 (rule C6); D16 Proposed, awaiting Amish: buy ISO 3864-1 and -4

claim: Smoke from FR panels is no worse than the platform accepts for patient spaces
law: Coroplast Firewall SDS: brominated FR < 5 %, antimony trioxide < 3 %; smoke includes hydrogen bromide and antimony oxides; IARC: antimony trioxide Group 2B (1989), trivalent antimony Group 2A (volume 131)
check: Corrosive and toxic smoke products are certain; their size relative to plain PP smoke is not quantified: to assess
closed_by: D11 Proposed, awaiting Amish: halogen-free FR search

claim: The FR grade does not shed burning drips
law: NFPA 701 TM1 pass criterion includes average flaming drip under 2 s (IntePro); EN 13501-1 d-class not found for twinwall
check: Supplier pass reports cover the NFPA criterion only; d-class and drip in a room-corner test (NFPA 286): to assess

claim: Ballast bags do not create a slip or lifting hazard
law: A 5 kg bag is far under the NIOSH load constant (23 kg); water bags can leak onto clinical floors
check: Fixed by rule B1: sand or gravel in a sealed bag inside the foot tray; water only double-bagged in a lipped tray
closed_by: Fix F11 (rule B1)

claim: Mixed P12 and P18 panels share joints
law: Shared clip grid
check: v0.1 heights (150, H/2, H - 150) gave no common middle clip; v0.2 grid 150 and 1050 for P12, plus 1650 for P18, shares two of three
closed_by: Fix F12 (clip_heights v0.2)
